To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the optimal structures of optimal matrix variables for a wide range of MIMO optimization problems can be derived by using a single framework, i.e., matrix-monotonic framework.

(i) The optimal structures of the transmit covariance matrix, receive covariance matrix, and the beamforming matrix can be obtained in closed-form for the three cases of CSI conditions; (ii) The optimal structures for the three cases are the same; (iii) The optimal structures are the same as that of the optimal structures of a single-input single-output (SISO) system; (iv) The optimal structures can be interpreted by the optimal structures of SISO systems.

the optimal structures of matrix variables in MIMO transceiver optimization can be determined by solving single-variable matrix-monotonically constrained optimization problems, and these optimal structures can be exploited to simplify the associated optimization problems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimal design of MIMO transceivers with imperfect CSI and/or norm-bounded channel estimation errors, which is of practical importance in wireless communications.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the optimal matrix variables of the MIMO transceiver design under the above-mentioned constraints are all of the form $A=UD$ where $U$ is a unitary matrix and $D$ is a nonnegative definite diagonal matrix.

the optimal structures of matrix variables are always diagonalizable, and the optimal diagonalizable structures of matrix variables in all three cases can be derived by solving a series of single-variable optimization problems.

the optimal structure of the optimal matrix variable in each of the cases above is diagonalizable with the diagonal elements being monotonically increasing with the diagonal elements of the channel covariance matrix, i.e., the matrix-monotone property.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the optimal structures for the matrix variable of the MIMO transceiver design problems are diagonalizable and the optimal diagonalizable matrices can be derived in a closed-form expression.
the matrix-monotomic optimization framework is applicable to a wide variety of MIMO transceiver design problems.

, under all the above-mentioned CSI conditions and power constraints, matrix-monotonicity can be used to simplify the optimization problems and the optimal structures can be derived analytically, and the resulting optimal structures can be used to design transceivers with good performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the three cases, the optimal structure for the optimal matrix variable is a diagonal matrix.
, in the single-variable case, the optimal structures of matrix variables can always be obtained by a simple diagonal scaling of the matrix variables.

matrix-monotonicity can be used to derive optimal structures of the matrix variables of the optimization problems, which can lead to substantial performance gains and also reveal underlying physical insights.
